minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard Monty Tech and DPW FY22 budgets, and a draft warrant letter; no budget votes taken.
minutes.summary: The committee heard Monty Tech's FY22 budget presentation, including a federal ESSER II offset to Lunenburg's assessment and the funding cliff it creates for FY23. It then heard the new DPW director's first budget presentation, with a new facilities technician and seasonal cemetery laborers, and questioned snow and ice funding and Chapter 90 use. The committee also discussed the warrant letter and draft warrant articles, received a finance director update on health insurance stabilization, and approved prior minutes before adjourning.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no budget votes; it heard Monty Tech's FY22 budget and its use of federal ESSER II money to offset member-town assessments.
Monty Tech said the offset creates a funding cliff in FY23, and that it is also using excess and deficiency funds to hold down the assessment increase.

The new DPW director presented a first budget with a facilities technician and seasonal cemetery laborers; members questioned snow and ice funding, which was running over its level-funded appropriation.
Members asked that the parks and cemetery commissions review and vote on their DPW budget lines before they come to the committee.
A draft warrant letter will be emailed to members for written comments, and the committee prefers to vote on it March 25.

why_it_matters: Lunenburg's Monty Tech assessment is being held down this year by one-time federal money, so the town may face a larger assessment increase in FY23 when it ends.
Snow and ice spending above its level-funded appropriation, and new DPW positions, bear on the town budget (mostly taxes) that voters will be asked to approve at Town Meeting.
watch_next: The committee's vote on the warrant letter, preferred for March 25.
Next week's meeting: town side personnel information, then public access, sewer and administration budgets.
